investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. No preemption victims exist on those nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and never progresses to a state where the eval runner can collect vmIdPresent or remoteState evidence. This is a cluster-capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity was recently narrowed or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may have been excluded. This would compound the capacity problem but is not independently evidenced in the supplied packet.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) failed to release resources from a previous run, those slots would remain occupied. No cleanup failure evidence is present in the packet, so this is speculative.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. No preemption victims exist on those nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and never progresses to a state where the eval runner can collect vmIdPresent or remoteState evidence. This is a cluster-capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-16 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept the pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 preemption victims available and no other eligible nodes, every remote-agent pod creation attempt is immediately marked Unschedulable by the scheduler. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure that prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent creation step, so no evidence can be collected and the expected-output contract cannot be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims, meaning all VM slots are occupied by existing workloads or leaked pods (highest evidence strength)

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift causing 4 of 6 nodes to be ineligible, artificially reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and making quota exhaustion more likely (supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector')
Cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata-peerpods-capable nodes in time, or autoscaling disabled/misconfigured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster tooling shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are NOT fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the quota-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission-controller failure would need to be investigated.
If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on a subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling contention rather than sustained quota exhaustion.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with similar messages, it would indicate a broader cluster-wide scheduling problem rather than one specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type.

If the node affinity/selector rules in the pod spec were recently changed to exclude 4 nodes (e.g., by a config or deployment change), that would shift the primary cause from quota exhaustion to misconfiguration — this would be supported by finding a relevant change in the pod spec or node labels not present in the current evidence.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded (e.g., they are a different node pool without kata support), then the affinity configuration is correct and the root cause remains purely quota exhaustion on the 2 valid nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes and fails with a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add an eval that detects stuck or zombie remote-agent pods (pods in non-Running, non-Completed states for longer than a configurable TTL) and reports their count and age as evidence, enabling proactive cleanup before quota exhaustion occurs.

Add an eval that validates the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods against the actual set of cluster nodes, failing if fewer than a minimum number of nodes match the selector — this would catch label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool to a critical size.

Consider adding a pre-flight check within the remote-agent-create eval runner branch that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available before attempting pod creation, and surfaces a distinct SKIP or WARN status with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.
